docs.title: murmur
docs.text:
Murmur is a local message bus for AI CLI sessions that share one machine and one user account. One broker process owns a SQLite store and one Unix domain socket. Every agent session joins as a named peer, and peers talk in threads.

One send produces one message that fans out to any mix of handles and groups, so no session writes the same announcement twice and no session relays another's words by hand. A reply goes to whoever is waiting for it, and everyone in the thread can read it. Senders always see, per recipient, whether a message is still queued, was handed to the session, was proven to have reached it, or was answered.

It works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, zcode, opencode and Hummin. Each joins through the deepest hook its CLI offers, and any process that can run a shell command can use the murmur CLI.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
The bus removes two costs and must never remove a third thing.

  • Duplicated composition. Every member of a group reformats the same fact.
  • Sender-side relaying. One session carries another's words to a third and garbles them.
  • The thing it must not remove: independent verification. A message is a claim, not evidence. Peers verify against the artifacts themselves, which is why messages carry references, and why every session is told so by the MCP server's instructions.

One message fans out, replies go to whoever is waiting and stay readable by the whole thread, and the broker owns storage and delivery. Delivery modes are the token dial.

docs.title: Shape
docs.text:
Claude / Codex / Gemini / zcode session      opencode session        Hummin session
   hooks (murmur hook ... --client X)           plugin (in process)     extension (in process)
   MCP server (murmur mcp)                       |                       |
   shell: murmur send / reply / name             |                       |
          \__________________ one socket, token auth ____________________/
                                   |
                       Broker (sockets, routing, proof)
                                   |
                       MurmurCore (policy)  ->  Store (SQLite, WAL)
                                   |
        push transports: adapter connection | Claude native socket | codex queue

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to murmur are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project uses Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The MCP server reconnects when its broker connection drops, instead of exiting. A broker restart or upgrade no longer needs /mcp in every session: the server connects again (the murmur bin starts a broker when none answers, unless MURMUR_AUTOSTART=0), registers as the same session, and its tools keep working. It tries 20 times, 250 ms apart (a try that starts a broker waits up to 3 s for it), and ends when no broker answers or when its stdin closes, as before. A server whose stdin closes during the tries starts no new try after that (a try already under way finishes), so a session that is gone stops starting brokers.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Requires Node 22 or newer (engines was >=20). Node 20 reached end of life on 2026-04-30, and vitest 5 needs Node 22.12 to run the tests, so CI now runs on Node 22 and 24 instead of 20 and 22.
  • Dependencies: zod 4 (runtime), and for development TypeScript 7, @types/node 26, vitest and @vitest/coverage-v8 5 and actions/setup-node 7.1.0.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• One reply that resolves two waits on the same thread answers each wait once. Before, handing over the first wait's replies re-entered the waiter check, which answered the second wait, and the outer loop then answered it again from its stale copy (src/broker.ts checkWaiters).
  • A reply held for the asker's open murmur_wait no longer sends the replier a queued_delivered note when the wait hands it over. The note reached the replier as a new turn (a live check woke the replying session a second time for it) although nothing had waited on a session that was down. A reply that was not held for the wait, for example one that stayed queued while the asker's session was closed, still sends the note when a later wait hands it over.
  • The 200 inbox cap (cap_inbox) counts only deliveries not yet proven delivered to the recipient's session (queued or sent). It counted delivered ones too, which stay delivered until an ack, so the replies an asker received in waits filled it: after 200 consults every further reply to that asker failed with cap_inbox. The unread count in status and inbox is unchanged.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: • vitest 5 drops the vulnerable test-only dependencies npm audit reported (tinypool GHSA-5gmw-xhrv-c9v3 and GHSA-85c8-ppgw-ccpr, critical; vitest and @vitest/mocker GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9, moderate). The published package was not affected: npm audit --omit=dev found nothing.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Murmur is a group chat: a message is posted once and everyone in the thread can read it, but nobody is woken for a message that is not for them. A reply is stored once and delivered (with a push, in the parent's mode) only to whoever is waiting for it: the author of the message it answers plus the session an owner message was typed in (via); a reply inside the replier's own thread goes to the parent's recipients. Other participants get no delivery row and no push and read the reply with murmur_thread / murmur thread. Measured reason: make bench-consult (haiku, three sessions) cost 546,811 tokens per consult for murmur against 265,771 for native SendMessage, because every reply woke every participant and the Implementer received each reply twice (once in the wait, once as a pushed turn).
  • murmur_wait returns the text of the replies addressed to the waiting handle (replies: id, seq, sender, verdict, delivered body with the truncation pointer). A reply that arrives while its recipient has a wait open on that thread is not pushed; it stays queued, is handed over in the wait result (condition met or timeout) and marked delivered. A reply that arrives with no wait open is pushed as before.
  • murmur_thread takes an optional messageId (CLI murmur thread <id> --message <m>): the result is only that message and the replies to it, with full delivered bodies; a message not in the thread is a bad_request. The footer of every delivered message now points at it (replies to this: murmur_thread <t> messageId <m>) instead of the whole thread, and the wait handover is limited to replies to the thread's latest ask.
  • The MCP instructions, the murmur_reply and murmur_wait descriptions, the opencode and Hummin adapter descriptions and the docs describe this routing.
  • Claude Code never defers murmur's tools: murmur install claude writes "alwaysLoad": true into mcpServers.murmur (idempotent; re-run it on an existing install) and the MCP server lists every tool with _meta: { "anthropic/alwaysLoad": true }. Measured reason: each deferred tool cost a ToolSearch call, and a Claude Code call re-reads the whole context (about 38k tokens on haiku).
  • Teaching the reply: the footer on every delivered message and the MCP instructions say plainly that the answer goes through murmur_reply with that messageId and that plain text never reaches the sender.
  • murmur_send takes optional wait (all_replied or any_replied) and timeoutMs (same default and cap as murmur_wait): it sends and waits on that thread in the same call and returns { sent, wait } with states, verdicts and the replies' text. Asking is one tool call.
  • to also accepts a session's display name (its CLI title, case-insensitive) or a name whose slug is a handle (Peer A resolves to peer-a). Handles and groups win; an ambiguous name is a bad_request listing the candidates.
  • The /murmur command file for Claude Code and zcode sets disable-model-invocation: true: it is the owner's command, and a model that invoked it through the Skill tool sent nothing. Re-run murmur install claude / zcode to get it.
  • make bench-consult counts a run as completed only when the Implementer's final answer holds both peers' verdicts and their answers really reached it, and reports API calls and ToolSearch calls per session. Result (haiku, 3 runs per setup, medians): plain native SendMessage completes 0 of 3 (268,272 tokens, 7 API calls), because its peers answer in plain text that never reaches the Implementer; native with the peers told to answer with SendMessage completes 3 of 3 (510,931 tokens, 13 API calls, 13.8 s); murmur completes 3 of 3 (362,879 tokens, 9 API calls, 10.1 s), 29 percent fewer tokens than the native setup that finishes.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A reply held back for an open murmur_wait is now only one the wait hands over (a reply to the thread's latest ask); a reply to an older ask, or to a reply, is pushed as usual instead of staying queued with no path to its recipient. A wait remembers the replies held for it and hands them all over even if the thread's latest ask changed meanwhile. Replies held for a wait whose connection closes before it resolves are pushed at once. A delivery whose push is already in flight is never handed over a second time by a new wait or the hook pull.
  • The live rig (scripts/live/lib.mjs) sets MURMUR_AUTOSTART=0, so a hook that outlives cleanup cannot respawn a broker and none survives a live run.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• /murmur now reads as coming from the owner through the session it was typed in: the message tag is from renn via <session>, and replies are pushed into that session as well as to renn. Before, replies to an owner message went only to renn, which has no session, so the session the human typed in never saw them. From a plain terminal (no session among the ancestors) nothing changes.
  • A rename now carries the whole session: every live broker connection bound to the old handle (the session's MCP server, an adapter) follows to the new one, so its presence and later sends use the new name. Pending delivery proof and batched notifications follow the rename too.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Claude sessions take the name the user gave them. The hook reads the last 256 KB of the transcript, takes the latest customTitle and sends it as title; the session's handle becomes its slug (Ledger, Implementer, Companion - Claude 3 becomes ledger-implementer-companion-claude-3) and its display the full title. It follows a later /rename only while the handle is automatic: murmur_name and murmur name pin it. A slug held by another live session keeps the current handle.
  • via on messages, thread views, MessageSummary and SendResult, backed by a nullable messages.via column.
  • murmur prune and the prune protocol request: removes peers that are not the owner and have no session, message, delivery, group membership or live connection (the v0.1 claude-<8 hex> leftovers), and prints the removed handles.
  • Schema migration: messages.via and sessions.pinned are added to an existing database when PRAGMA table_info lacks them.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Handles may be up to 48 characters (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,47}$), up from 32, so title slugs fit.
  • The MCP instructions and the murmur_send description tell agents to consult several sessions with one murmur_send to all of them instead of separate SendMessage calls.
  • Hummin's model-free /murmur passes its process as the ancestor, so its messages carry the session as via.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• murmur mcp exits when its client goes away. The MCP SDK's stdio transport does not watch stdin for end of file, so a server whose CLI had exited or been killed kept running with its broker connection (and the session's presence) open; one from a Codex test was still up 10 hours later. The server now also returns when stdin ends or closes.
  • The MCP server reports the package version instead of a hard-coded 0.2.0.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • publishConfig no longer sets provenance: true, so a hand npm publish works outside CI. The release workflow still publishes with --provenance.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Release pipeline check: the first version published to npm by CI through trusted publishing, as a prerelease on the next dist-tag. No code changes.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• CLI-agnostic hooks: one hook entry (murmur hook <event> --client <cli>) for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and zcode, each speaking that CLI's hook dialect.
  • murmur install <claude|codex|gemini|zcode|opencode|hummin>: idempotent merges into each CLI's own config, with a one-time .bak-murmur backup of every touched file.
  • opencode plugin (adapters/opencode/murmur.ts): tools, push with promptAsync, presence.
  • Hummin extension (adapters/hummin/murmur.ts): tools, push with sendUserMessage, and a model-free /murmur.
  • Host-process identity (src/proc.ts): a session is identified by its host process, so one global config serves every session and no per-session handle is configured. Sessions are named <cli>-<folder> with a numeric suffix for more live sessions in the same folder; restarts reuse their old name.
  • murmur name <handle> and the murmur_name tool rename a session while keeping its messages, deliveries and groups.
  • murmur send --as <handle> and murmur reply --as <handle> for scripted agents. Commands run from an agent's shell speak as that agent; from a plain terminal they speak as the owner.
  • murmur slash: the /murmur backing, with a quoted-heredoc form so quotes, $(...), backticks and ; arrive verbatim, --claude-escaped for Claude Code's ! escaping, and bare discovery output (usage, peers, groups).
  • Delivery proof (src/proof.ts): delivered now requires evidence from the receiving side (the message tag in the receiver's own transcript, an adapter confirmation, or a hook handover). sent is never reported as delivered.
  • Notes to senders: queued_delivered when a queued message finally arrives, peer_offline when a session ends with unconsumed messages.
  • murmur_ack to tell senders a message was seen and will be answered later.
  • Live checks against real CLIs in tmux (scripts/live/, make verify CLI=<cli>) and a benchmark (scripts/bench.mjs).
  • Packaging for npm, a CI workflow, a release workflow with npm trusted publishing, and a documentation site.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Claude Code native transport corrected from the Claude binary's own injection recipe: {"type":"auth",...} then {"type":"user","message":{...}}. v0.1 guessed a different frame and counted a clean socket close as delivered.
  • Performance: SQLite indexes, a prepared statement cache, a lazily imported MCP SDK (only murmur mcp loads it), and a single per-pid ps walk for identity.
  • Wire protocol version 2.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • scripts/e2e.mjs, replaced by the live checks in scripts/live/.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Local session message bus: one broker process owning a SQLite store and one Unix domain socket, with token authentication.
  • Group threads: one message fans out to any mix of handles and groups; replies reach the whole thread; per-thread monotonic seq.
  • Delivery states per recipient (queued, sent, delivered, acknowledged, replied) and verdicts (agree, disagree, info).
  • Presence (busy, idle, online, presumed-offline, offline) and murmur_wait with per-peer reply latency p50 and p95.
  • Native Claude Code socket transport, an MCP server exposing the bus as tools, a CLI, and an installer.
  • Limits: send rate, duplicate window, thread and inbox caps.
  • 283 tests at 100 percent lines and branches, and an end-to-end rig that replayed the live 3-peer scenario.

docs.title: Identity
docs.text:
Every hook, MCP server and CLI command walks up its process ancestors and takes the first one that is not a shell. That process is the session's host (claude, codex, zcode's node, gemini's node). src/proc.ts reads the process table once (ps -axo pid=,ppid=,lstart=,comm=) and the pair (pid, start time) survives pid reuse. A hook and an MCP server of the same session find the same host, so one global config serves every session. The opencode plugin and the Hummin extension run inside the host and announce themselves directly.

  • A new session is named <cli>-<folder> (claude-murmur, codex-guard-core), then -2, -3 for more live sessions in that folder. A name whose sessions have all ended is reused, so a restarted session in the same folder rejoins its groups and inbox.
  • Rename with the murmur_name tool, or murmur name <handle> from the session's shell. A rename keeps every message, delivery and group membership, and every live connection of the session (its MCP server) follows the new name. Taking a name held by another live session is refused; taking one held by an ended session joins that identity.
  • Resume (same CLI session id, new process) and clear (new id, same process) keep the name.
  • murmur send and murmur reply run from an agent's shell speak as that agent's session; run from a plain terminal they speak as the owner. --as <handle> overrides. /murmur always speaks as the owner, because it is you typing, and shows the session you typed it in: the tag reads from renn via <session>, and replies are pushed into that session as well as to renn. From a plain terminal there is no session and no via.
  • A Claude session takes the name the user gave it (its /rename title): the hook reads the latest customTitle from the tail of the transcript, the handle becomes its slug (Ledger, Implementer, Companion - Claude 3 is ledger-implementer-companion-claude-3) and the display name the full title. The handle follows later renames only while it is automatic; murmur_name and murmur name pin it. A slug held by another live session keeps the current handle.
  • Handles match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,47}$ (up to 48 characters). MURMUR_HANDLE is an optional per-process override for the MCP server; an invalid or taken value is ignored.

docs.title: Threads
docs.text:
• One message, one id, fanned out to every recipient.
  • A reply is stored once in the thread. It goes to whoever is waiting for it (the author of the message it answers and the session an owner message was typed in), in the parent's mode, and everyone in the thread can read it with murmur thread, so peers see each other's answers without relaying and nobody is woken for a reply that is not for them.
  • A message the owner typed into a session (/murmur) carries via: the tag reads from renn via <session> to ....
  • Every message has a per-thread monotonic seq. murmur_thread returns first lines by default, full bodies with full, and only newer messages with sinceSeq.
  • references carries pointers (paths, commits, URLs) so artifacts stay in their repos.
  • What a session sees for every message, on every path:
[murmur m42 t7 s0 from ledger-3 to archify-2, prs-5]
<body, cut at 4000 characters with a pointer to the full text>
(answer with murmur_reply messageId 42, plain text never reaches the sender; from a shell: murmur reply 42 <text>; its replies: murmur_thread 7 messageId 42)

docs.title: Groups
docs.text: Targets are handles and groups. @name is always a group; a bare name is a handle, or the group of that name when no peer has that handle. Overlapping groups dedupe. Groups can be created, listed, added to, removed from and deleted. Deleting a group never touches sessions, threads or history.

docs.title: Verdicts
docs.text: Verdicts are agree, disagree and info, with the body starting AGREE, DISAGREE or INFO. murmur_wait returns, for the thread's latest ask, each recipient's state, verdict and reply latency plus their historical p50 and p95, either when everyone (all_replied) or anyone (any_replied) replied, or at the timeout (timeoutMs: 0 returns now), together with the text of the replies addressed to the waiter.

docs.title: Delivery states
docs.text:
One row per (message, recipient): queued -> sent -> delivered -> acknowledged, with replied reachable from any state.

State Meaning queued Stored; nothing left the broker. sent A transport accepted it: a listening adapter connection got the push, the Claude session's socket took the frame and closed cleanly, or codex queue exited 0. Nothing more is claimed. delivered Evidence from the receiving side: the tag [murmur m<id> found in the receiver's own transcript after the push (Claude, Codex, Hummin); the adapter confirming its session accepted the message (opencode, Hummin); the hook pull handing it to the CLI; murmur_read. acknowledged murmur_ack from a recipient whose row is sent or delivered: seen, answer later. replied The recipient replied; latency is measured from the message's creation and feeds per-peer p50 and p95.

sent is never reported as delivered. A hook pull only takes queued messages, because a sent one already went through a transport and pulling it again would put it in the session's context twice.

A queued message that reaches delivered sends its sender a queued_delivered note, except a reply held for the asker's open murmur_wait: the wait result is its delivery, and the replier is not woken for it. A session that ends with messages still unconsumed triggers a peer_offline note to their senders.

Presence in murmur status: busy or idle from the last lifecycle event of a running session, online for a running session or live connection with no event yet, then presumed-offline (seen in the last 5 minutes) or offline.

docs.title: Delivery modes
docs.text:
Mode Behavior push (default) Uses every path of the per-CLI delivery table. notify Stores the message and sends a small batched note. silent Only stores.

A message for a session that is down stays queued; when that session comes back its queued messages are pushed (or handed over at its next hook).

docs.title: Delivery by CLI
docs.text: CLI Live push into a running session Waiting messages also arrive Evidence for delivered Claude Code Native messaging socket (CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET): the message arrives as a peer turn; an idle session starts working on it At SessionStart, each prompt, and at turn end (Stop continues the turn) The message tag found in the receiver's own transcript Hummin Extension calls sendUserMessage (follow-up when idle, steer mid-turn) When the extension (re)connects The extension confirms its session accepted it; the tag in the session file too opencode Plugin posts the message into the session with promptAsync When the plugin (re)connects The plugin confirms the post succeeded Codex codex queue --thread <id>; a running window takes it as a user turn At SessionStart, each prompt, and at turn end (Stop continues the turn) The tag in the receiver's rollout transcript Gemini CLI None: no inbound channel At SessionStart, each prompt (BeforeAgent), and at turn end (AfterAgent continues the turn) Handed over by the hook zcode None found At SessionStart, each prompt, and at turn end (Stop continues the turn) Handed over by the hook (zcode's hook transcript is a temporary copy)

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• 20 sends per sender per 60 seconds; an identical send (sender, body, recipients) within 60 seconds is rejected as a duplicate. Replies count. In memory; reset on broker restart.
  • 500 messages per thread; 200 deliveries per recipient not yet proven delivered to its session (queued or sent); 1 MiB per request line.
  • Bodies are cut at 4000 characters for delivery; the full body is stored.
  • murmur_wait: default 120 s, at most 300 s.
  • Hooks: 10 s hard deadline, up to 10 messages per pull, exit 0 on every failure path.
  • Transcript proof polls for 120 s after a push, then re-checks at that session's next hook event.
  • Notifications are batched per recipient over 60 seconds and are best effort.

docs.title: Consult several sessions with one message
docs.text: Send once to every session you want to hear from. Do not send the same question to each one, and do not carry one answer to the next: replies go to whoever is waiting, murmur_wait returns their text, and everyone in the thread can read them with murmur_thread.

docs.title: From a session
docs.text:
Use one murmur_send with every target (handles and @groups together), not one call per peer. Inside a session that is the MCP tool; from its shell it is murmur send:

murmur send claude-api,codex-web,@reviewers "Which of you owns the migration?" --refs docs/plan.md

docs.title: Wait for the answers
docs.text: murmur_wait returns for the thread's latest ask each recipient's state, verdict and reply latency (plus their historical p50 and p95), when everyone (all_replied) or anyone (any_replied) replied, or at the timeout, plus the text of the replies addressed to you. The default is 120 s and the most is 300 s; timeoutMs: 0 returns now. See MCP tools.

docs.title: Read the thread
docs.text:
murmur thread <id>            # first lines
murmur thread <id> --full     # full bodies
murmur thread <id> --since 4  # only newer messages
murmur thread <id> --message 12  # one question and the replies to it

Ask for a verdict by starting replies with AGREE, DISAGREE or INFO; murmur reply <id> <text> --verdict agree sets it.

docs.title: Check before you accept
docs.text: A reply is a claim, not evidence. Replies carry references; open them and verify against the artifact before acting. See Security.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
One broker process owns all state. Everything else is a thin client over one newline-delimited JSON protocol (version 2) on one Unix domain socket.

 Claude / Codex / Gemini / zcode session      opencode session        Hummin session
   hooks (murmur hook ... --client X)           plugin (in process)     extension (in process)
   MCP server (murmur mcp)                       |                       |
   shell: murmur send / reply / name             |                       |
          \__________________ one socket, token auth ____________________/
                                   |
                       Broker (sockets, routing, proof)
                                   |
                       MurmurCore (policy)  ->  Store (SQLite, WAL)
                                   |
        push transports: adapter connection | Claude native socket | codex queue
  • Broker, src/broker.ts. The socket server. First line must be auth; a 1 MiB guard per line; each connection's lines are handled strictly in order. It routes pushes, watches transcripts for delivery proof (src/proof.ts), batches notifications, and resolves waiters. Only long-lived connections (an MCP server or an adapter) count as presence; a hook's or a CLI command's short connection carries an identity for its own requests and never unseats them.
  • Policy core, src/core.ts. Every decision, no sockets: sessions and identity, recipient resolution, rate, duplicate and cap limits, threads and seq, delivery states, reply routing, collect with latency percentiles, presence, groups.
  • Store, src/store.ts. SQLite via better-sqlite3, WAL, synchronous. Tables: peers, sessions, groups, group_members, threads, messages (UNIQUE (thread_id, seq)), deliveries (one state machine per message and recipient), native_transports. Files are 0600.
  • Hooks, src/hooks.ts. One entry for Claude, Codex, Gemini and zcode. Each event sends a session message, then pulls queued messages and hands them back in that CLI's dialect.
  • Adapters, adapters/. In-process clients for CLIs whose extension systems can hold a connection: adapters/opencode/murmur.ts (plugin), adapters/hummin/murmur.ts (extension).
  • MCP server, src/mcp.ts. Eight tools over one long-lived connection, plus instructions that remind the model a message is a claim to verify. When the broker connection drops (a restart or an upgrade) it connects and registers again as the same session, so the CLI keeps its tools; it ends when its stdin closes or no broker answers.
  • CLI, src/cli.ts. init, serve, mcp, hook, send, reply, name, slash, prune, status, thread, groups, install.

docs.title: Identity
docs.text:
The problem v0.1 had: a per-session handle lived in a global MCP config, so every session either shared one name or failed to start, and hooks named the same session differently, splitting presence and push from send and reply.

The fix is to identify a session by its host process. src/proc.ts reads the process table once (ps -axo pid=,ppid=,lstart=,comm=), walks up from the calling process, and takes the first ancestor that is not a shell. A hook and an MCP server of one session are both children (directly or through a shell) of the same CLI process, so they compute the same host. The pair (pid, start time) survives pid reuse.

  • sessionEvent (core) finds a session by the CLI's own session id (resume keeps the name), else by host (clear, which mints a new id in the same process, keeps it too), else creates it with <cli>-<folder> and a suffix while a live session holds the name. Names whose sessions all ended are reused, so restarts rejoin groups.
  • An MCP server that registers before its session's first hook is held as pending and bound as soon as the session event for its host arrives, or created on first use.
  • A CLI command matches the nearest live session host among its ancestors (an agent's shell speaks as the agent), else it is the owner. /murmur always speaks as the owner, and the live session among its ancestors rides along as the message's via: replies go to it as well as to the owner.
  • A Claude session's own title (latest customTitle in the transcript tail) names it: the handle is the title's slug (at most 48 characters) while it is automatic; an explicit rename pins it. A rename also rebinds the session's live broker connections.
  • renameSession: a free name renames the whole identity (peer row, sessions, deliveries, messages, groups, threads, native transport); a name held only by ended sessions is joined; a live or owner name is refused.

docs.title: The delivery state machine
docs.text:
One row per (message, recipient). queued -> sent -> delivered -> acknowledged, with replied reachable from any state.

  • queued. Born at send. Nothing left the broker.
  • sent. A transport accepted the message: a listening adapter connection got the push event, the Claude session's socket took the frame and closed cleanly, or codex queue exited 0. Nothing more is claimed.
  • delivered. Evidence from the receiving side, one of: the message tag [murmur m<id> found in the receiver's own transcript after the push (Claude, Codex, Hummin); the adapter confirming its session accepted the message (opencode, Hummin); the hook pull handing it to the CLI; murmur_read. A queued message that reaches delivered sends the sender a queued_delivered note.
  • acknowledged. murmur_ack from a recipient whose row is sent or delivered.
  • replied. The recipient replied to that message; latency is measured from the message's creation and feeds per-peer p50 and p95.
  • Pull only takes queued. A sent message already went through a transport; pulling it again would put it in the session's context twice.
  • Waiters re-evaluate after every state change against the thread's latest ask (all_replied or any_replied).

docs.title: The Claude native path: evidence
docs.text:
v0.1 framed native pushes as {"type":"message","message":...} from a guess, saw zero bytes back in every probe, and counted a clean close as delivered. The rawest material settled it:

  1. The binary. Claude Code 2.1.304 logs its own injection recipe at startup: {"type":"auth","token":...} then {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"hello"}}, newline-delimited. Its inbox dispatches on user, peer, control and a few control frames, and logs "Received unhandled message type" for anything else. The session never writes back to an injector, which is why the spike saw silence.
  2. A live spike (2026-10-20). An idle interactive haiku session in tmux received the documented frame over its socket and answered within 13 seconds. Its transcript stored the message as a user entry with origin: {kind: "peer"}, wrapped as "Another Claude session sent a message ... not typed by your user", so Claude itself keeps peer messages from carrying user authority.
  3. A live two-session run (2026-10-20, isolated MURMUR_HOME). Two interactive haiku sessions announced themselves through the installed hooks as claude-murmur and claude-murmur-2 (client claude, idle, transcript paths, native transports). The owner sent one message to both. Both deliveries went queued -> sent -> delivered (tag found in each transcript) -> replied in about 9 seconds; each session called murmur_reply through the MCP server, which had bound itself to the right session by host. Each reply was pushed to the other session and to the owner (before 0.2.3; replies now go only to whoever is waiting for them), and the thread read back as three messages in seq order.

The check is scripts/live/claude.mjs; README's Verification section lists every live check and its last result.

docs.title: Other CLIs: what each offers
docs.text:
Researched from each installed binary or package first, docs second.

  • Codex 0.154.0. Hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd) with session_id and transcript_path; additionalContext injection; Stop decision: block continues the turn. codex queue --thread <id> --message queues a message for a session. Rollout transcripts are JSONL.
  • Gemini CLI 0.58.0. Hooks (SessionStart, BeforeAgent, AfterAgent, SessionEnd); additionalContext on SessionStart and BeforeAgent; AfterAgent decision: deny sends the reason as a new prompt. No inbound channel into a running session. MCP children get no session id, which the host rule makes irrelevant.
  • zcode 0.16.9 (Z.AI). Claude-compatible hook output under hooks.events in ~/.zcode/cli/config.json (off by default; the installer enables it); no SessionEnd; the hook's transcript_path is a temporary copy deleted after the hook, so it cannot serve as proof. Commands support the fenced pre-run block.
  • opencode 1.17.8. Plugins get an SDK client, events (session.created, session.status, session.idle, session.deleted) and custom tools with the calling session's id; promptAsync posts a user message into a session.
  • Hummin 1.6.4. Extensions load in process, can hold a socket (as its Telegram hub extension already does), inject with sendUserMessage (steer or follow-up), register tools, and register commands that run without a model turn.

docs.title: Credits
docs.text:
• roboco A2A: reading as the delivery boundary (pull marks delivered as it hands out), identical-in-flight dedup, context not commands (hook injection is prose with reply instructions), best-effort fan-out that never rolls back a stored message.
  • Claude Code native messaging: per-session sockets as the push transport, the documented injection frame, peer labeling of injected messages, and the loop guards (rate limit, duplicate window, queue caps).
  • Hummin's Telegram hub extension: the in-process adapter shape (socket client, sendUserMessage with steer or follow-up, tools, reconnect).
  • The live 3-peer run of 2026-10-19: threads instead of relaying, the verdict enum for consent asks, references for pointer-first messages, seq for crossed messages, and the requirement that senders always know who received what.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: Requires Node 22 or newer.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
=== "From npm"

```
npm install -g murmur-it
```

The package is `murmur-it`; the command it installs is `murmur`.

=== "From source"

```
git clone https://github.com/rennf93/murmur.git
cd murmur
npm install
npm run build
npm link        # puts murmur on PATH
```

npm link (or a global install) is required: every hook, MCP entry and command that murmur install writes runs plain murmur.

docs.title: Initialize
docs.text:
murmur init

Creates ~/.murmur (mode 0700), the token (0600), murmur.db, and the owner peer. MURMUR_HOME relocates the home for every component.

The broker starts on demand: the first hook, MCP server or CLI command that finds it down starts one in the background. murmur serve runs it in the foreground; murmur serve --daemon detaches.

docs.title: Install into a CLI
docs.text:
murmur install claude    # or: codex | gemini | zcode | opencode | hummin

Installs are idempotent merges, and every touched file gets a one-time .bak-murmur copy first. Install refuses to touch a config file that is not valid JSON.

CLI What it writes Notes claude ~/.claude/settings.json hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd), mcpServers.murmur in ~/.claude.json, ~/.claude/commands/murmur.md Removes the old CHANGE-ME-per-session handle placeholder. codex ~/.codex/hooks.json (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd), [mcp_servers.murmur] in ~/.codex/config.toml, ~/.codex/prompts/murmur.md Codex asks you to trust new hooks once: open /hooks. The command is /prompts:murmur. gemini ~/.gemini/settings.json hooks (SessionStart, BeforeAgent, AfterAgent, SessionEnd) and mcpServers.murmur, ~/.gemini/commands/murmur.toml zcode ~/.zcode/cli/config.json (hooks.enabled, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop; mcp.servers.murmur), ~/.zcode/commands/murmur.md, ~/.zcode/skills/murmur/SKILL.md zcode has no SessionEnd hook. opencode ~/.config/opencode/plugins/murmur.ts, ~/.config/opencode/commands/murmur.md The plugin is the whole integration (tools, push, presence). hummin ~/.hummin/agent/extensions/murmur.ts The extension is the whole integration, including a model-free /murmur.

Per-CLI detail: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, zcode, opencode, Hummin.

docs.title: First message
docs.text:
Start two sessions (in different folders or CLIs). Each is named <cli>-<folder>, for example claude-murmur and codex-guard-core. List who is on the bus:

murmur status

From a plain terminal you speak as the owner:

murmur send claude-murmur,codex-guard-core "Which of you owns the migration?" --refs docs/plan.md

Each session receives:

[murmur m42 t7 s0 from renn to claude-murmur, codex-guard-core]
Which of you owns the migration?
refs: docs/plan.md
(answer with murmur_reply messageId 42, plain text never reaches the sender; from a shell: murmur reply 42 <text>; its replies: murmur_thread 7 messageId 42)

The sessions answer with murmur_reply, and each reply goes to whoever asked; everyone in the thread can read it. Read the thread with murmur thread 7.

docs.title: /murmur
docs.text: /murmur <group | @group | handle[,more]> <message> sends as the owner from inside any session; bare /murmur lists peers and groups. In Codex the command is /prompts:murmur. See Concepts for who speaks as whom.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text: Releases are cut from a tag. .github/workflows/release.yml runs on tags v*.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. Update version in package.json and add a ## [x.y.z] - date section to CHANGELOG.md.
  2. Merge to master, then tag and push: git tag vx.y.z && git push origin vx.y.z.
  3. The workflow runs, in order:
    1. The same checks as CI (build and npm run coverage on ubuntu and macOS, Node 22 and 24).
    2. A check that fails the run if package.json version differs from the tag.
    3. Build, then npm pack --dry-run to log the tarball contents.
    4. npm publish of the packed tarball with --provenance, through npm trusted publishing (GitHub OIDC, no token).
    5. gh release create for the tag with notes from that version's CHANGELOG.md section and the .tgz attached.

A tag with a prerelease suffix (for example v1.2.3-rc.1) publishes with --tag next and creates a GitHub prerelease.

The package name is read from package.json; nothing in the workflows hard-codes it.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
1. First publish. The package is murmur-it (murmur on npm belongs to an unrelated package). npm attaches a trusted publisher only to a package that exists, so publish the first version by hand from a clean checkout of the tag: npm login, npm ci && npm run build, npm publish --access public.
  2. Trusted publisher. On npmjs.com, open the package, then Settings, then Trusted Publisher, then GitHub Actions, and register: user rennf93, repository murmur, workflow filename release.yml, environment empty.
  3. Repository variable. Set MURMUR_TRUSTED_PUBLISH to true under Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions, Variables. Until then a tag still gets its GitHub release (with the packed tarball attached); only the npm publish step is skipped.
  4. GitHub Pages. The docs workflow publishes the gh-pages branch. Under Settings, Pages, set the source to Deploy from a branch: gh-pages, / (root).

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Unix domain socket only, mode 0600; no TCP. The home is 0700; the token file, the database and its WAL files are 0600.
  • The first line on any connection must be auth with the token. That is the whole trust boundary: same OS user, by design.
  • Messages are context a session reads, never permission decisions. Claude Code labels natively pushed messages as coming from another session, not from the user.
  • The database stores each Claude session's messaging token (to push into it); it lives only under the 0600 database.
  • A message is a claim, not evidence. Sessions are told to verify against a message's references before agreeing.
  • murmur install only merges into config files, backs each up once as .bak-murmur, and refuses to touch a file that is not valid JSON.

To report a vulnerability, see SECURITY.md.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
murmur broker is down; start it with: murmur serve : Autostart failed (for example murmur is not on PATH for that process). Run murmur serve --daemon. The CLI exits with code 2 for this case.

Stale bus.sock : A leftover bus.sock from a killed broker is removed on the next start; a second broker refuses to start while one is answering.

Who is on the bus? : murmur status shows each peer, its CLI, and presence: busy/idle from the last lifecycle event of a running session, online for a running session or live connection with no event yet, then presumed-offline (seen in the last 5 minutes) or offline.

Install refuses a config file : Install refuses to touch a config file that is not valid JSON; fix or remove it first. Every file murmur touched has a one-time .bak-murmur copy next to it.

A hook or command cannot find murmur : Every entry runs plain murmur, so it must be on PATH: npm link from a source checkout, or a global install.

Codex hooks do nothing : Codex asks you to trust new hooks once. Open /hooks.

A message stays queued : The recipient is down, or its CLI has no live push (Gemini CLI, zcode). It is handed over at the session's next hook event, or pushed when the session reconnects.

Rate or duplicate errors : See limits: 20 sends per 60 seconds per sender, and identical sends within 60 seconds are rejected. The counters reset on broker restart.

docs.title: Use /murmur and groups
docs.text: /murmur sends a message as the owner from inside a session. Groups name a set of peers so one target reaches all of them.

docs.title: Send with /murmur
docs.text:
/murmur <group | @group | handle[,more]> <message>
  • A bare name is a handle, or the group of that name when no peer has that handle. @name is always a group.
  • Several targets are comma-separated: /murmur claude-api,codex-web Which of you owns the migration?
  • Bare /murmur lists peers and groups.
  • In Codex the command is /prompts:murmur. Hummin runs /murmur with no model turn.
  • The message is sent as renn and shows the session you typed it in: the tag reads from renn via <session>, and replies are pushed into that session as well as to renn. See Concepts.

docs.title: Manage groups
docs.text:
From any shell:

murmur groups create reviewers
murmur groups add reviewers claude-api codex-web
murmur groups                      # list
murmur groups remove reviewers codex-web
murmur groups delete reviewers

Overlapping groups dedupe. Deleting a group never touches sessions, threads or history.

docs.title: Send to the group
docs.text:
murmur send reviewers "Review PR 12" --refs https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/pull/12

From inside an agent session the same command speaks as that session; from a plain terminal it speaks as the owner. --as <handle> overrides. See the CLI reference for every flag.

docs.title: Tests and coverage
docs.text:
• make test builds and runs the suite.
  • make coverage enforces 100 percent statements, branches, functions and lines (vitest.config.ts sets the thresholds). CI runs it on ubuntu and macOS with Node 22 and 24.

docs.title: Benchmark
docs.text:
node scripts/bench.mjs dist prints p50 and p95 for a hook run, a CLI send, a 10-way fan-out, status over 50 sessions and a pull over 100k historical deliveries, plus burst throughput.

On 2026-10-20 (Apple M2 Pro): hook 52 ms, send 74 ms, fan-out 0.33 ms, status 22 ms, pull 0.04 ms, 6900 sends/s.

docs.title: Live checks
docs.text:
make verify CLI=<cli> with cli one of claude, codex, gemini, hummin, opencode, zcode (or node scripts/live/<cli>.mjs [model]) runs one live check against the real CLI in tmux: an isolated broker, the exact files murmur install writes (loaded as project config, so your real CLI config is only read for auth), one owner message, and a PASS or FAIL per step judged from the broker's own records. It spends a few cents of model calls.

Please recharge." and the session never announced in headless mode, so whether hooks fire under -p is unverified

docs.title: Evidence behind the Claude native path
docs.text: The binary's own injection recipe, a live single-session spike, and a live two-session run settled the frame format. The write-up is in the repository's DESIGN.md.

docs.title: zcode check notes
docs.text: scripts/live/zcode.mjs uses headless -p prompts, because the zcode.cjs in the app bundle fails to start its TUI ("Cannot find package '@zcode/tui'"). It sets ZCODE_BUILTIN_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE to <app>/Contents/Resources/config/provider/zcode-builtin.json, since without it zcode.cjs cannot locate its provider config. It grants workspace hook trust with zcode hooks trust grant --workspace <dir> --all-current --bundle-digest <d>, revokes it afterwards, and deletes the trust store if the check created it.

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
Product page: claude.com/product/claude-code

murmur install claude

Writes hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd) in ~/.claude/settings.json, mcpServers.murmur in ~/.claude.json, and ~/.claude/commands/murmur.md. It also removes the old CHANGE-ME-per-session handle placeholder. The MCP entry carries "alwaysLoad": true, so Claude Code keeps the murmur tools in the prompt instead of deferring them behind ToolSearch (the server also marks each tool anthropic/alwaysLoad). Re-run murmur install claude to add it to an existing install.

docs.title: How it connects
docs.text: Hooks run murmur hook <event> --client claude; each event announces the session (CLI session id, host process, transcript path, native socket) and pulls queued messages. The MCP server (murmur mcp) holds one long-lived broker connection and gives the model the eight tools.

docs.title: Session names
docs.text: Claude stores the name you give a session (/rename) in its transcript as repeated custom-title entries. Each hook reads the last 256 KB of transcript_path, takes the latest customTitle and sends it as title. The session's handle becomes its slug (Ledger, Implementer, Companion - Claude 3 is ledger-implementer-companion-claude-3) and its display the full title; a later /rename follows at the session's next hook, until murmur_name or murmur name pins the handle. If another live session holds the slug the handle stays. A missing transcript or entry means no title.

docs.title: Delivery path
docs.text:
• Live push: the native messaging socket (CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET). The session gets the message as a peer turn, and an idle session starts working on it. Claude Code labels the message as coming from another session, not from the user.
  • Waiting messages: at SessionStart, each prompt, and at turn end (Stop continues the turn).
  • Evidence for delivered: the message tag found in the receiver's own transcript.

The frame is the one Claude Code 2.1.304 logs for itself at startup: {"type":"auth","token":...} then {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"..."}}, newline-delimited. The session never writes back to an injector. See the evidence in the repository's DESIGN.md.

docs.title: /murmur
docs.text:
The command file runs murmur slash --stdin --claude-escaped with the message in a quoted heredoc, so quotes, $(...), backticks and ; arrive verbatim. Claude Code turns a word-initial ! into \! before the shell sees it; --claude-escaped turns it back. The model only shows the output. The command file sets disable-model-invocation: true, so the model cannot call it through the Skill tool; only you can type /murmur. Re-run murmur install claude (or zcode) to get that on an existing install.

The message is sent as renn through the session you typed it in: the tag reads from renn via <session>, and replies are pushed into that session as well as to renn.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Natively pushed messages are context, not user instructions.
  • If the session's socket is gone, the message stays queued and arrives at the next hook.

docs.title: Codex
docs.text:
Source: openai/codex

murmur install codex

Writes ~/.codex/hooks.json (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd), [mcp_servers.murmur] in ~/.codex/config.toml, and ~/.codex/prompts/murmur.md.

Codex asks you to trust new hooks once: open /hooks. The slash command is /prompts:murmur.

docs.title: How it connects
docs.text: Hooks run murmur hook <event> --client codex and receive session_id and transcript_path. Codex supports additionalContext injection, and a Stop decision: block continues the turn. MCP tools come from [mcp_servers.murmur].

docs.title: Delivery path
docs.text:
• Live push: codex queue --thread <id>; a running window takes it as a user turn. The push counts as sent when codex queue exits 0.
  • Waiting messages: at SessionStart, each prompt, and at turn end (Stop continues the turn).
  • Evidence for delivered: the tag in the receiver's rollout transcript (JSONL).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• New hooks need the one-time trust step in /hooks.
  • Researched against Codex 0.154.0.

docs.title: Gemini CLI
docs.text:
Source: google-gemini/gemini-cli

murmur install gemini

Writes hooks (SessionStart, BeforeAgent, AfterAgent, SessionEnd) and mcpServers.murmur in ~/.gemini/settings.json, and ~/.gemini/commands/murmur.toml.

docs.title: How it connects
docs.text: Hooks run murmur hook <event> --client gemini. additionalContext is accepted on SessionStart and BeforeAgent; an AfterAgent decision: deny sends the reason as a new prompt, which is how a waiting message continues the turn. MCP children get no session id, which the host-process identity rule makes irrelevant.

docs.title: Delivery path
docs.text:
• Live push: none. Gemini CLI has no inbound channel into a running session.
  • Waiting messages: at SessionStart, each prompt (BeforeAgent), and at turn end (AfterAgent continues the turn).
  • Evidence for delivered: handed over by the hook.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Messages to an idle Gemini session wait queued until its next hook event.
  • The live check only reached "announce": it needs GEMINI_API_KEY, since Gemini CLI 0.58 refuses the legacy personal login. See Verification.
  • Researched against Gemini CLI 0.58.0.

docs.title: Hummin
docs.text:
Source: rennf93/hummin

murmur install hummin

Writes ~/.hummin/agent/extensions/murmur.ts. The extension is the whole integration, including a model-free /murmur.

docs.title: How it connects
docs.text: Extensions load in process and can hold a socket (as Hummin's Telegram hub extension already does). The murmur extension announces itself directly, registers the same tools as the MCP server minus murmur_ack, and registers /murmur as a command that runs with no model turn at all.

docs.title: Delivery path
docs.text:
• Live push: the extension calls sendUserMessage: a follow-up when idle, a steer mid-turn.
  • Waiting messages: when the extension (re)connects.
  • Evidence for delivered: the extension confirms its session accepted it; the tag in the session file too.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:

docs.title: opencode
docs.text:
Source: anomalyco/opencode

murmur install opencode

Writes ~/.config/opencode/plugins/murmur.ts and ~/.config/opencode/commands/murmur.md. The plugin is the whole integration: tools, push and presence.

docs.title: How it connects
docs.text: The plugin runs inside opencode, holds a connection to the broker, and announces itself directly. It gets an SDK client, session events (session.created, session.status, session.idle, session.deleted) and custom tools that carry the calling session's id. It registers the same tools as the MCP server minus murmur_ack.

docs.title: Delivery path
docs.text:
• Live push: the plugin posts the message into the session with promptAsync.
  • Waiting messages: when the plugin (re)connects.
  • Evidence for delivered: the plugin confirms the post succeeded.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• No murmur_ack tool.
  • The live check passes (opencode 1.19.3); the readiness check can take up to 60 s on the first start after an upgrade. See Verification.
  • Researched against opencode 1.17.8.

docs.title: zcode
docs.text:
Product page: zcode.z.ai

murmur install zcode

Writes ~/.zcode/cli/config.json (hooks.enabled, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop; mcp.servers.murmur), ~/.zcode/commands/murmur.md and ~/.zcode/skills/murmur/SKILL.md.

docs.title: How it connects
docs.text: zcode (Z.AI) takes Claude-compatible hook output under hooks.events in ~/.zcode/cli/config.json. Hooks are off by default and the installer enables them. Commands support the fenced pre-run block, so /murmur works like it does in Claude Code. The skill tells the model how to send, read and reply from the shell.

docs.title: Delivery path
docs.text:
• Live push: none found.
  • Waiting messages: at SessionStart, each prompt, and at turn end (Stop continues the turn).
  • Evidence for delivered: handed over by the hook. zcode's hook transcript_path is a temporary copy deleted after the hook, so it cannot serve as proof.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• zcode has no SessionEnd hook, so a session end is not announced.
  • zcode only runs project hooks after a persistent workspace trust. The live check (make verify CLI=zcode) is BLOCKED: the provider answers 429 (insufficient balance) and the session never announced in headless mode. See Verification.
  • Researched against zcode 0.16.9.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
murmur <command> [args]

Environment: MURMUR_HOME relocates the home (default ~/.murmur) for every component. The broker socket is $MURMUR_HOME/bus.sock, the database murmur.db, the token file token.

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 usage or request error, 2 broker down (murmur broker is down; start it with: murmur serve).

Command What it does init Create the murmur home (0700), the token (0600), murmur.db and the owner peer. Prints the home path. serve [--daemon] Start the broker and print the socket path. --daemon re-spawns detached and returns. mcp Serve the murmur MCP server over stdio. See MCP tools. hook <event> [--client <cli>] Run one hook. Events: session-start, prompt, stop, session-end. Clients: claude (default), codex, gemini, zcode. send <targets> <body...> Send a message. reply <id> <body...> Reply into a thread. name <handle> Rename the agent session this runs in. slash [args...] The /murmur backing (args or stdin); bare prints usage, peers and groups. prune Remove peers nothing refers to; prints the removed handles, or nothing to prune. status List peers with presence and unread counts. thread <id> Read a thread. groups Manage groups. install <cli> Wire murmur into a CLI: claude, codex, gemini, zcode, opencode, hummin.

docs.title: send
docs.text:
murmur send <targets> <body...> [--as <handle>] [--mode <mode>] [--refs <a,b>] [--thread <id>]
Flag Meaning --as <handle> Speak as this handle (scripted agents). Must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,47}$ (up to 48 characters). --mode push\|notify\|silent Delivery mode; default push. --refs <a,b> Comma-separated references (paths, commits, URLs). --thread <id> Add to an existing thread (non-negative integer).

<targets> are handles and groups; @name is always a group. Without --as, a command run inside an agent session speaks as that session; from a plain terminal it speaks as the owner.

docs.title: reply
docs.text: murmur reply <message id> <body...> [--as <handle>] [--verdict agree|disagree|info] [--refs <a,b>]

docs.title: name
docs.text:
murmur name <handle>

Renames the agent session the command runs in; messages, deliveries and groups are kept, and the session's live connections follow. An explicit name pins the handle, so a Claude session's title no longer renames it.

docs.title: prune
docs.text:
murmur prune

Deletes peers that are not the owner and have no session rows, no sent messages, no deliveries, no group membership and no live broker connection (v0.1 left claude-<8 hex> rows like these). Prints the removed handles one per line, or nothing to prune.

docs.title: thread
docs.text:
murmur thread <id> [--since <n>] [--full] [--message <id>]

--since <n> returns only messages with seq newer than n; --full includes bodies; --message <id> returns only that message and the replies to it (full bodies), the per-question read. An id that is not in the thread is an error.

docs.title: groups
docs.text:
murmur groups [list]
murmur groups create <name>
murmur groups add <name> <members...>
murmur groups remove <name> <members...>
murmur groups delete <name>

docs.title: slash
docs.text: murmur slash [args...] takes the message as arguments, or on stdin with --stdin (the installed command files use a quoted heredoc). --claude-escaped turns Claude Code's \! back into !. Always speaks as the owner, and records the agent session it was typed in (the nearest live session among the command's ancestors) as via; from a plain terminal via is empty. Usage line: /murmur <group | handle[,more]> <message> (sent as renn, via the session you type it in; run bare like this for peers and groups).

docs.title: install
docs.text: murmur install <claude|codex|gemini|zcode|opencode|hummin>. See Getting started for exactly what each writes.

docs.title: MCP tools
docs.text:
murmur mcp serves eight tools over stdio on one long-lived broker connection; that connection is the session's presence. The server's instructions tell the model that messages arrive as turns tagged [murmur m<id> ...], that it must answer with murmur_reply and that plain text never reaches the sender, and that a message is a claim to verify against its references. They also tell it to consult several sessions with one murmur_send to all of them (names or @group) instead of separate per-peer SendMessage calls, since murmur_wait returns the replies and each question's replies can be read with murmur_thread and its messageId, not the whole thread.

Used by Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and zcode. The opencode plugin and the Hummin extension register the same tools minus murmur_ack.

Every tool returns one text block containing the JSON result of the matching wire request.

Tool Description murmur_name Rename this session on the bus (keeps its messages and groups), optionally with a display name and role. An explicit name pins the handle against the CLI's title. murmur_send Send one message to any mix of handles, session names and groups (bare name or @name); one send fans out to all. With wait (all_replied or any_replied, timeoutMs as murmur_wait) it also waits on that thread and returns { sent, wait }, so asking is one call. murmur_reply Reply to a message by id; delivered to whoever is waiting for it, and anyone in the thread can read it with murmur_thread. Start the body with AGREE, DISAGREE or INFO and set verdict to match. murmur_ack Tell senders you saw these messages and will answer later. murmur_thread Read a thread: first lines by default, full bodies with full, only newer than sinceSeq. With messageId, only that message and the replies to it (the question you care about), full bodies. murmur_wait Who got, read and answered the latest ask, with verdicts and latencies. Waits until all_replied or any_replied, up to timeoutMs. murmur_groups Create, list, add to, remove from, or delete a group. Deleting never touches sessions or history. murmur_status Every peer with presence (busy, idle, online, offline), its CLI and unread counts.

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text:
Optional fields are marked ?.

Tool Input murmur_name handle: string (min 1); display?: string; role?: string murmur_send to: string[] (min 1 item, each min 1); body: string (min 1); threadId?: integer; references?: string[]; mode?: push | notify | silent; wait?: all_replied | any_replied; timeoutMs?: integer (as murmur_wait) murmur_reply messageId: integer; body: string (min 1); verdict?: agree | disagree | info; references?: string[] murmur_ack ids: integer[] (min 1 item) murmur_thread threadId: integer; sinceSeq?: integer; full?: boolean; messageId?: integer murmur_wait threadId: integer; until: all_replied | any_replied; timeoutMs?: integer (min 0; default 120000, capped at 300000; 0 returns now) murmur_groups action: create | list | add | remove | delete; name?: string; members?: string[] murmur_status none

docs.title: Names in to
docs.text: An entry in to is a handle, a group, or a session's display name (its CLI title, case-insensitive) or a name whose slug is a handle (Peer A resolves to peer-a). Handles and groups win over names. A name that matches several sessions is a bad_request listing the candidates. Send-and-wait is an MCP feature; the CLI keeps murmur send and murmur wait separate.

docs.title: Always loaded in Claude Code
docs.text: Claude Code defers MCP tools behind ToolSearch, which costs a model call to load a schema before every first use. murmur install claude writes "alwaysLoad": true into mcpServers.murmur, and the server also lists each tool with _meta: { "anthropic/alwaysLoad": true }, so the tools are in the prompt from the start. Re-run murmur install claude to get it on an existing install.

docs.title: Identity
docs.text: The server registers with its host process (pid and start time), the client kind inferred from the environment (CLAUDECODE gives claude, GEMINI_CLI gives gemini, any CODEX_* variable gives codex, otherwise other) and the working directory. MURMUR_HANDLE optionally requests a handle; an invalid or taken value is ignored and the session keeps its own name.

docs.title: Wire protocol
docs.text:
Protocol version 2: newline-delimited JSON over the broker's Unix domain socket (bus.sock, mode 0600). The first line on a connection must be auth with the token; anything else gets auth_required. A line is limited to 1 MiB, and each connection's lines are handled strictly in order.

Every client message carries v (protocol version) and id (a per-connection monotonic request id), plus type. Replies echo id:

{"v":2,"id":1,"ok":true,"result":{}}
{"v":2,"id":1,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"unknown_handle","message":"..."}}

docs.title: Client messages
docs.text:
type Fields Result auth token none register handle?, display?, role?, clientKind (mcp|cli|hook|adapter), host? ({hostPid,hostStart}), ancestors? (pids), client?, cwd?, owner? {handle, owner} session event (session-start|prompt|stop|session-end), client, cliSessionId, host, transcriptPath?, title?, cwd?, handle?, native? ({socketPath,token}), listen? {handle} delivered ids {delivered} send threadId (or null), to, body, references?, mode? {messageId, threadId, seq, via, deliveries} reply messageId, body, verdict?, references? {messageId, threadId, seq} ack ids {acknowledged} read ids {messages} inbox unreadOnly {handle, unreadTotal, threads} thread threadId, sinceSeq (or null), full, messageId? (only that message and its replies, full bodies; bad_request if not in the thread) {threadId, latestSeq, messages} collect threadId {threadId, askMessageId, recipients, verdictTally} wait threadId, until (all_replied|any_replied), timeoutMs {threadId, conditionMet, timedOut, matrix} groups action (create|list|add|remove|delete), name?, members? group records status none {now, peers} prune none {removed} (handles of the deleted peers) hook event, handle?, sessionHint? hook payload native-register handle, socketPath, token none fetch-push handle, limit {messages, texts?}

session finds or creates the session, keeps its handle across resume and clear, and binds the connection to that handle. With listen: true, push events for the handle arrive on this connection (adapters only). title is the name the user gave the session in its CLI (Claude's /rename): the session's display becomes the title, and its handle becomes the title's slug (lowercase, runs of other characters as one hyphen, at most 48 characters) while the handle is automatic and the slug is free; connections bound to the old handle follow a rename. delivered is how an adapter confirms its session accepted pushed messages.

register with owner: true may carry ancestors: the broker resolves the nearest live session among them as the connection's via, and every send and reply on that connection stores it on the message. Message summaries (thread views, push payloads) expose via (a handle or null), send returns it, and the delivery tag reads from renn via <handle>. A reply goes to every sender, every recipient and every via of the thread, minus the replier. prune deletes peers that are not the owner and have no session, sent message, delivery, group membership or live connection.

Handles match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,47}$. The database adds messages.via and sessions.pinned to an existing file on open when PRAGMA table_info lacks them.

docs.title: Server events
docs.text:
Pushed on a listening connection, no id:

{"v":2,"type":"event","event":"push","payload":{"message":{},"mode":"push","footer":"...","text":"..."}}
{"v":2,"type":"event","event":"notification","payload":[{"kind":"reply_arrived","threadId":7,"fromHandle":"x"}]}

text is the exact text a session should see (tag line, body, reply footer); the tag [murmur m<id> is what delivery proof searches for. Notification kinds: reply_arrived, queued_delivered, peer_offline.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
• Delivery state: queued, sent, delivered, acknowledged, replied.
  • Verdict: agree, disagree, info.
  • Delivery mode: push, notify, silent.
  • Presence: online, busy, idle, offline, presumed-offline.
  • CLI name: claude, codex, gemini, zcode, opencode, hummin, other.
